timing_contract:
# E28 completed-contract cost probe

Run only after both native and real WASM qualification have completed. Reuse their frozen generated artifacts read-only. Both variants run the same Node v22 probe and WebAssembly memory observation hook. Module loading, fixture construction, explicit GC, independent semantic checking, byte comparison, and evidence writes are outside timing. Timed exports retain every complete JavaScript String or Uint8Array; pipeline timing also includes native import, strict union with empty, the certainty check, result consumption, and disposal of the imported input. Retained pipeline meshes remain alive through memory observation.

The matched successful contract is binary/ASCII export of 0, 1, or 256 separated unit cubes. Five alternating pairs cover each encoding/size. Every process measures first output separately from 64 warm outputs (four for 256 cubes); outputs remain retained. Compare full constructed-input and output bytes across variants and repeats. Independent integer boundaries, outward winding, paired edges, and signed volume validate the represented boxes; triangle count is an additional deterministic-artifact check.

The baseline has no native JavaScript import, and its string exceptions do not satisfy the new typed-failure contract. Therefore candidate-only import/composition/export pipelines and typed-error creation receive five absolute observations each, with no baseline speed ratio. The same 0/1/256 fixtures and encodings qualify the pipelines. Error repetitions exercise eight distinct triggers, retain all 520 host Error objects per process, and check their native categories and nested construction causes. Complete first-cycle error records, including stack strings, are retained; stacks are not required to have identical execution histories.

Record raw elapsed nanoseconds, Node process memory, WebAssembly linear-memory high-water observations, and externally observed peak RSS. These are not Rust allocation counts or live-heap bounds. External containment is 120 seconds and 64 GiB address space per process; it does not add a public total-work, memory, or cancellation contract. Preserve all samples, including unfavorable ones. This patch expands usable contracts and makes no optimization or full-corpus performance claim.
